module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Imaginary part of $\prod_{k=0}^n (1 + k \cdot i)$, $i = \sqrt{-1}$

*References:*
- [A105751](https://oeis.org/A105751)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Complex Filter Topology Nat

namespace OeisA105751

/--
The primary defining sequence `a`.
a n is the imaginary part of $\prod_{k=0}^n (1 + k \cdot i)$, where $i = \sqrt{-1}$.
-/
noncomputable def a (n : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  let productTerm (k : ℕ) : ℂ := 1 + (k : ℂ) * I
  Int.floor (((Finset.range (n + 1)).prod productTerm).im)

/-- Term theorems verifying the first few values of the sequence against the official OEIS b-file -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_0 : a 0 = 0 := by
  delta a; norm_num [Finset.prod]

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 1 := by
  delta a; norm_num [Finset.prod]

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 3 := by
  delta a; norm_num [Finset.prod]

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 0 := by
  delta a; norm_num [Finset.prod]

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = -40 := by
  delta a; norm_num [Finset.prod]

/--
Numerical calculation suggests that a similar division holds in this case.
Type 1: primes p that do not divide any element of the sequence {$a(n)$}.
In this case, unlike in A105750, the set of type 1 primes is empty;
that is, every prime p divides some term of this sequence.

Note: The triangular number n*(n+1)/2 divides $a(n)$ (see A164652).
In particular, if $p$ is an odd prime then $p$ divides $a(p)$. For $p=2$, $2$ divides $a(4)=-40$.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem prime_divides_some_term (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, (p : ℤ) ∣ a n := by
  sorry

/--
Moll's conjecture 5.5 extends to this sequence and takes the form:
(i) the $2$-adic valuation $\nu_2(a(n)) \sim n/4$ as n -> oo.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
    "https://github.com/KitaKen1/oeis-a105751-two-adic/blob/a9692d90078c4dff1478acaaa70be2fba06a3ef9/lean/OeisA105751TwoAdicFC.lean#L980-L985"]
theorem conjecture :
    Tendsto (fun n ↦ (4 : ℚ) * (padicValInt 2 (a n) : ℚ) / (n : ℚ)) atTop (nhds 1) := by
  sorry

/--
Moll's conjecture 5.5 extends to this sequence and takes the form:
(ii) for the other primes of type $2$, the p-adic valuation
$\nu_p(a(n)) \sim n/(p - 1)$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$.

(Type 2 primes consists of primes p == 1 (mod 4))
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture.variants.moll_p_mod_4_eq_1 {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (h_mod : p % 4 = 1) :
    Tendsto (fun n ↦ ((p - 1 : ℚ) * (padicValInt p (a n) : ℚ)) / (n : ℚ)) atTop (nhds 1) := by
  sorry

end OeisA105751

reformulations.difference: The definition takes Int.floor of the imaginary part, whereas OEIS defines the sequence directly as the imaginary part of the product.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every factor 1 + k*i is a Gaussian integer, so the product's imaginary part is an integer and taking its floor changes nothing. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, a_is_imaginary_part proves the exact equality after casting a n to ℝ, and a_definition_iff proves equivalence for every proposed integer value.

reformulations.difference: The source's ν₂(a(n)) ∼ n/4 is expressed as convergence of 4*ν₂(a(n))/n to 1 in ℚ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The standard topology on ℚ is induced from ℝ, so convergence to the rational number 1 is equivalent in either space. Eventually n is nonzero, and 4*ν₂(a(n))/n is exactly the quotient ν₂(a(n))/(n/4). The biconditional with real-valued Asymptotics.IsEquivalent is proved as main_asymptotic_iff in scratch. Separately, a(n)=0 iff n=0 or n=3 was proved using the checked linked proof, so the valuation's zero default and division at n=0 affect only finitely many initial terms.

reformulations.difference: The source's ν_p(a(n)) ∼ n/(p−1) is expressed as convergence of (p−1)*ν_p(a(n))/n to 1 in ℚ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a prime p, p−1 is nonzero; the subtraction in the declaration is rational subtraction. The normalized expression equals ν_p(a(n))/(n/(p−1)), and rational convergence is equivalent to real convergence. This biconditional is proved as variant_asymptotic_iff in scratch. The hypothesis p % 4 = 1 selects precisely the conjectured 'other' type-2 primes described by OEIS, with p=2 handled separately.

review.notes: Checked all nine declarations. Exact computation through a proven Gaussian-integer representation matched every official b-file entry for n=0..450. prime_divides_some_term is trivial via a 0 = 0, even without primality, but OEIS explicitly makes the same unrestricted claim; this textbook statement is therefore faithful. The exact cited 2-adic proof compiled against this checkout, and #print axioms reported only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], supporting the solved status. The consulted OEIS source still presents the odd-prime variant as conjectural. OEIS HTML endpoints were Cloudflare-blocked, so its official data mirror was used. Lean checks and logs are under /workspace/review/, principally scratch.lean, zero_boundary.lean, and linked-proof-check.jsonlog.
